item.title: MODBEACON, XRING XQUIC, Zimbra XSS, and WP-SHELLSTORM Drive Threat Digest
item.content:encoded:
New MODBEACON RAT Uses gRPC Streaming for Encrypted C2 Traffic — Must Read

China-linked Silver Fox is using a new Rust-based RAT called MODBEACON, delivered through fake software installers and SEO poisoning, to target organizations in Asia. The malware uses encrypted gRPC streaming based on Xray/V2Ray transport to maintain stealthy C2, load plugins in memory, execute commands, and persist on infected hosts.

  • The China-linked cybercrime group Silver Fox has been attributed to a new Rust-based remote access trojan called MODBEACON.
  • QiAnXin said a mid-June 2026 campaign delivered MODBEACON through counterfeit software installers distributed via SEO campaigns, targeting technology, education, and state-owned enterprises in Asia.
  • MODBEACON is a memory-resident remote implant that can fetch additional modules, run operator commands, maintain encrypted communications with attacker infrastructure, and set persistence using scheduled tasks.
  • QiAnXin said MODBEACON uses a separated loader and beacon, injectable configuration, a plugin-based architecture, and gRPC tunnel streaming based on transport reused from the Xray/V2Ray open-source anti-censorship proxy framework.
  • The campaign’s command-and-control infrastructure is hosted on Amazon and Cloudflare’s Content Delivery Network.

Zimbra urges customers to patch critical web client XSS flaw — Must Read

Zimbra is urging customers using the Classic Web Client to upgrade to ZCS 10.1.19 to fix a critical stored XSS flaw that can be triggered by malicious emails and expose session or mailbox data. The bug was reported by Google’s Threat Analysis Group, raising concern because Zimbra flaws have repeatedly been targeted by state-backed hackers.

  • Zimbra released Zimbra 10.1.19 to patch a critical stored cross-site scripting flaw affecting the Classic Web Client used to access the Zimbra Collaboration suite.
  • Attackers can exploit the flaw through specially crafted emails that execute malicious code when opened, potentially enabling theft of session data, account settings, or mailbox information.
  • Zimbra said the issue only impacts users of the Classic Web Client and urged those customers to upgrade to ZCS v10.1.19 as soon as possible.
  • The vulnerability has not yet received a CVE ID, and Zimbra has not said it is being exploited in the wild.
  • The flaw was reported by Google's Threat Analysis Group, and the article notes that Zimbra security issues have frequently been exploited by Russian state-sponsored hackers in recent years.

Exposed Hacker Server Reveals WP-SHELLSTORM Backdooring Thousands of WordPress Sites — Must Read

Researchers found an exposed server belonging to the WP-SHELLSTORM cybercrime crew, revealing tools and logs used to mass-scan over 1.4 million sites and backdoor thousands of mostly vulnerable WordPress installations. Site owners should urgently patch affected WordPress/Joomla plugins and hunt for webshells such as .bd.php, .wp-log.php, and .brq-*.php.

  • Researchers found an exposed server belonging to the WP-SHELLSTORM operation that contained about 800MB of webshells, exploit scripts, scan results, command history, and command-and-control settings.
  • The operation targeted more than 1.4 million domains in its lists, but confirmed compromises were much lower, with Ctrl-Alt-Intel identifying 25,195 sites with compromise evidence and SOCRadar reporting more than 5,700 active webshells.
  • The most productive exploit in the campaign was CVE-2026-3844 in the WordPress Breeze caching plugin, which the crew used against more than 45,000 targets and claimed had backdoored over 17,000 sites.
  • The exposed files showed the crew also ran an earlier campaign against corporate Java systems using CVE-2021-29441 in Nacos to steal configuration files containing cloud keys, database passwords, and Alipay RSA private keys.
  • The article advises administrators to patch affected WordPress and Joomla plugins, upgrade and secure Nacos, disable risky unauthenticated endpoints, search for webshell filenames, and check suspicious kworker-like processes.

Hackers Use Fake Microsoft Entra Passkey Enrollment to Gain Microsoft 365 Access — Should Read

A threat actor tracked as O-UNC-066 is using phone calls and a fake Microsoft Entra passkey enrollment flow to trick Microsoft 365 users into approving access and letting attackers register their own passkeys. The campaign abuses organizations’ push toward passkey adoption to gain persistent account access for data extortion.

  • A threat actor tracked by Okta as O-UNC-066 is targeting organizations with voice-based fake security requests that prompt Microsoft 365 users to enroll a new Microsoft Entra passkey.
  • The campaign has targeted the food and beverage, technology, healthcare, automotive, construction, and aviation industries.
  • The phishing kit imitates the Microsoft passkey enrollment process while allowing the threat actor to register their own passkey against the victim’s Microsoft account.
  • The operator-controlled PHP phishing kit can adapt the victim’s experience in real time to different multi-factor authentication requirements, including time-based one-time passwords, push notifications with number matching, and SMS one-time passwords.
  • Okta said a threat actor linked to O-UNC-066 has operated a data leak site since April 2026 under the name Pink, which Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 tracks as CL-CRI-1147 and describes as affiliated with The Com.

China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force — Should Read

SentinelOne says China- and India-linked hackers ran separate espionage campaigns against Balochistan Police systems in Pakistan from 2024 to 2026, in some cases compromising the same networks. The intrusions exposed sensitive law enforcement and citizen data, reflecting China’s concerns over threats to its workers in Pakistan and India-Pakistan regional rivalry.

  • SentinelOne reported that hacking groups linked to China and India conducted separate, unconnected espionage operations against Pakistani law enforcement between February 2024 and April 2026.
  • The activity centered on the Balochistan Police, whose compromised systems reportedly held criminal records, biometric and fingerprint data, personnel files, hotel and tenant registrations linked to national identity records, and citizen complaints.
  • SentinelLabs assessed that China-linked interest was primarily driven by protecting Chinese nationals in Pakistan tied to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, while India-linked activity was likely tied to India-Pakistan rivalry.
  • SentinelLabs said a China-linked operator compromised the Balochistan Police Complaint Management System by planting malware disguised as a portal update that showed a fake “update complete” message while infecting visitors’ devices.
  • The China-nexus assessments were anchored by tools including PlugX and ShadowPad, while the India-nexus intrusions were tied with lower confidence to TAG-179, overlapping with clusters called Bitter and Mysterious Elephant.

Study of 281 Free Android VPN Apps Finds Traffic Leaks, Unencrypted Data, and Tracking — Should Read

A study of 281 popular free Android VPN apps found widespread security and privacy failures, including traffic and DNS leaks, unencrypted data, tracking, weak encryption, and even hijackable VPN configurations. The main takeaway is that many free VPNs do not provide the protection they promise and may expose users to greater risk.

  • Researchers tested 281 popular free Android VPN apps from the Google Play Store with a system called MVPNalyzer and found that apps with at least one flagged problem had more than 2.4 billion installs.
  • The study found that 29 apps leaked user traffic outside the encrypted tunnel, including DNS lookups, and 61 apps sent some data in plain text that could be read by someone watching the network.
  • Five apps downloaded their configuration files without encryption, allowing an attacker on the same network to rewrite the file and redirect the VPN connection to a server they control.
  • The researchers found that 76 apps sent the device Advertising ID, more than 80% of the apps contacted known advertising and tracking servers, and one app sent exact GPS coordinates.
  • Among 108 apps with OpenVPN configuration files examined, only one followed every security best practice measured, while some used weak or outdated encryption or disabled encryption entirely.

Unpatched XRING Flaw in XQUIC Lets Remote Clients Crash HTTP/3 Servers — Should Read

A flaw dubbed XRING in Alibaba’s XQUIC HTTP/3 library lets unauthenticated remote clients crash affected servers with a small amount of valid QPACK traffic. All releases through v1.9.4 are affected and no patch is available, so operators should disable QPACK dynamic tables or HTTP/3 until a fix ships.

  • FoxIO researcher Sébastien Féry disclosed an unpatched XQUIC flaw called XRING on July 8 that lets a remote unauthenticated client crash an HTTP/3 server with about 260 bytes of legal QPACK traffic.
  • Every XQUIC release through v1.9.4 is affected, and as of July 10 there is no fixed release and no CVE.
  • The flaw is in XQUIC’s ring buffer handling when growing the QPACK dynamic table, where one copy path uses the new buffer capacity instead of the old one and can trigger an unsigned size_t underflow.
  • XQUIC is embedded by other servers that support HTTP/3, including Tengine, Alibaba’s Nginx-based web server, which FoxIO says fronts Alibaba cloud and CDN sites including Taobao and Alipay.
  • Until a fix is available, operators can set SETTINGS_QPACK_MAX_TABLE_CAPACITY to 0 to disable QPACK’s dynamic table or disable HTTP/3 entirely.

The Email With Nothing to Scan: A 1 MB HTML Attachment That Renders Its Own Phishing Page — Should Read

A phishing email used a large self-contained HTML attachment to render a credential-harvesting page locally, leaving no URL for gateways to reputation-check and exceeding deep inspection limits. The key lesson is that authenticated email and clean static scans are not enough; detection must rely on sender behavior, message context, and post-delivery remediation.

  • An external first-time Gmail sender delivered a one-line email directing the recipient to open a roughly 1 MB HTML attachment named like a full report.
  • SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC all passed because the message was genuinely sent through Gmail and signed with a gmail.com key.
  • The HTML attachment rendered its phishing page locally in the browser, leaving no malicious URL in the message for a secure email gateway to extract and reputation-check.
  • Static scanning returned a clean verdict, while deeper content analysis failed because the HTML file exceeded the analyzer's processing limit.
  • The article says the useful detection signals were the first-time external sender, no prior correspondence, high-risk flag, minimal body text, and large attachment.

From 17,000 to 1.1 Million Assets: How Lumen Technologies Rebuilt Exposure Management at Scale — Optional

Lumen Technologies used Axonius to reconcile data from more than 40 disconnected systems, revealing its asset inventory was vastly undercounted and growing known devices from about 17,000 to 1.1 million. The key takeaway is that trusted asset data is the foundation for effective exposure management, faster zero-day response, and risk-based remediation.

  • Lumen Technologies used the Axonius asset intelligence platform to reconcile data from more than 40 disconnected systems into one trusted view.
  • Lumen’s known cyber assets increased from about 17,000 in existing inventories to 500,000 after initial reconciliation and approximately 1.1 million devices currently.
  • Lumen’s team can now identify systems affected by a critical vulnerability, determine whether they are externally exposed, and establish ownership within minutes.
  • Lumen built an Application Posture Dashboard within Axonius to evaluate risk at the application level by correlating CMDB relationships with control coverage, vulnerability data, and end-of-life status.
  • Lumen’s leadership used Axonius-generated visibility to support cloud migration decisions, increase security spending to roughly 10 times its previous level, and provide board-level reporting on asset coverage, EDR deployment, and compliance insights.
